records.title: 2018 Canada–China merchandise trade baseline
records.changed: Global Affairs Canada reported C$103.2 billion in two-way merchandise trade for 2018: C$27.6 billion in Canadian exports to China and C$75.6 billion in imports from China.

records.title: First Canada–China Economic and Financial Strategic Dialogue
records.changed: Ministers and China’s State Councillor concluded the first substantive strategic economic and financial dialogue. Published outcomes covered trade and investment, agriculture, financial supervision and future sector-policy discussions.

records.title: Canada requests WTO consultations on China’s canola restrictions
records.changed: Canada opened WTO dispute DS589 over restrictions affecting canola seed from two Canadian companies and enhanced inspections on Canadian canola seed. A panel was established in July 2021.

records.title: Canada changes sensitive-export treatment for Hong Kong
records.changed: Canada announced immediate treatment of sensitive exports to Hong Kong on the same basis as exports to mainland China, including prohibiting sensitive military items. Canada also suspended its Hong Kong extradition treaty.

records.title: Canada announces Huawei and ZTE telecommunications restrictions
records.changed: Canada announced intended prohibitions on designated Huawei and ZTE network equipment and services. Its policy set transition dates for existing 5G and 4G equipment and proposed a broader telecommunications-security framework.

records.title: Canada orders divestitures of three critical-mineral investments
records.changed: Following national-security reviews, Canada ordered three foreign investors to divest specified interests in Power Metals, Lithium Chile and Ultra Lithium. The announcement concerned investments in Canadian critical-mineral companies, including lithium.

records.title: Canada directs TikTok blocking on federal government devices
records.changed: The government’s Chief Information Officer directed TikTok blocking on covered Government of Canada devices from 5 p.m. EST on February 27. A public announcement described removal from government-issued mobile devices from February 28.

records.title: Canada implements Chinese EV surtax and finalizes steel and aluminum coverage
records.changed: A 100% surtax on covered China-origin EVs took effect on October 1, 2024. A separate 25% surtax on specified Chinese steel and aluminum goods took effect on October 22.

records.title: China applies additional tariffs to selected Canadian agricultural and fishery products
records.changed: China applied additional 100% duties to covered canola oil, meal and peas and 25% duties to specified pork, fish and seafood products. Canada requested WTO consultations on the same day.

records.title: China imposes preliminary anti-dumping duty on Canadian canola seed
records.changed: China announced a 75.8% preliminary anti-dumping duty on Canadian canola seed on August 12, with entry into force on August 14. This was distinct from the March duties on meal, oil and peas.

records.title: Huawei added to the U.S. Entity List
records.changed: BIS added Huawei and specified non-U.S. affiliates to the Entity List, requiring licences for covered exports, re-exports and in-country transfers of items subject to the Export Administration Regulations.

records.title: Phase One agreement enters into force
records.changed: The agreement signed on January 15 entered into force on February 14. It combined commitments on agriculture, financial services, intellectual property and technology transfer with a bilateral implementation and dispute-resolution mechanism.

records.title: Forced-labour import presumption takes effect
records.changed: The Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act introduced a rebuttable presumption against U.S. imports made wholly or partly in Xinjiang, or by listed entities. The law had been enacted on December 23, 2021.

records.title: Advanced computing and semiconductor export controls
records.changed: BIS introduced controls on advanced chips, semiconductor manufacturing and related activity. Implementation was staged: manufacturing-item controls on October 7, specified U.S.-person support on October 12, and advanced-computing controls on October 21.

records.title: Economic and financial working groups launched
records.changed: The U.S. Treasury and Chinese authorities launched separate Economic and Financial Working Groups for regular policy discussions and information exchange. Treasury and China’s finance ministry led one group; Treasury and the central bank led the other.

records.title: Section 301 tariff increases on covered Chinese goods
records.changed: The finalized review raised Section 301 duties on covered Chinese goods, including a 100% rate for electric vehicles and 25% for EV batteries. The 2024 tranche applied from September 27; other increases had later dates.

records.title: Outbound Investment Security Program takes effect
records.changed: Treasury’s final rules introduced notification requirements and prohibitions for specified U.S.-person investments connected to China, Hong Kong or Macau in semiconductors, quantum technologies and artificial intelligence.

records.title: Connected-vehicle rule: effective date and phased prohibitions
records.changed: The rule took legal effect on March 17. Covered software and certain China- or Russia-linked manufacturers face model-year 2027 restrictions; covered connectivity hardware requirements generally apply from model year 2030.

records.title: Treasury announces its first outbound-investment penalty
records.changed: Treasury announced that a US$200,000 civil penalty had been imposed in July 2026 for failure to notify a covered investment by a controlled foreign entity in a Chinese embodied-AI company.

records.title: COINS implementation proposal would expand outbound-investment rules
records.changed: Treasury proposed updates implementing the COINS Act. The proposal covered additional technologies, including high-performance computing, hypersonics and biotechnology, alongside changes to existing outbound-investment rules.

records.title: Canada implements steel and aluminum countermeasures
records.changed: Canada imposed 25% surtaxes on listed U.S. steel and 10% on listed aluminum and other goods after U.S. Section 232 duties. The C$16.6 billion coverage figure describes reference trade, not revenue collected.

records.title: Canada and the U.S. remove the 2018 steel and aluminum tariffs
records.changed: Following the May 17 joint understanding, Canada removed its retaliatory surtaxes effective May 20 as the United States lifted its steel and aluminum duties. The understanding included monitoring and provisions addressing import surges.

records.title: Roadmap for a Renewed U.S.–Canada Partnership
records.changed: The leaders set a joint agenda covering supply-chain resilience, critical minerals, batteries, climate, security and pandemic cooperation. They committed to renew energy cooperation and strengthen the bilateral opioids action plan.

records.title: Canada announces a 20-year NORAD modernization plan
records.changed: Canada announced C$38.6 billion over 20 years on an accrual basis for NORAD modernization. Priorities included surveillance, command and communications, air weapons, infrastructure and research supporting continental defence with the United States.

records.title: Canada and the U.S. launch an Energy Transformation Task Force
records.changed: The leaders launched an initially one-year task force to accelerate clean-energy cooperation, including critical minerals, electric vehicles, grids and nuclear energy. Their joint agenda also addressed semiconductor supply chains and advanced packaging.

records.title: First joint critical-mineral funding for Fortune and Lomiko projects
records.changed: Canada announced up to C$7.5 million for Fortune Minerals and C$4.9 million for Lomiko Metals. U.S. Defense Production Act awards added US$6.4 million and US$8.4 million respectively for critical-mineral development work.

records.title: Canada’s automobile countermeasures enter into force
records.changed: Canada applied 25% tariffs to non-CUSMA-compliant fully assembled U.S. vehicles, and to the non-Canadian, non-Mexican content of CUSMA-compliant U.S. vehicles. The measure took effect at 12:01 a.m. EDT on April 9.

records.title: Canada removes most March 2025 countertariffs
records.changed: Canada removed the 25% countertariffs on the March 4 C$30 billion list and March 13 C$14.2 billion list of other goods. Steel, aluminum and automobile countermeasures remained at that point.

records.title: United States Surtax Order 2026 takes effect
records.changed: CBSA’s implementation notice applies 15%, 25% or 50% surtaxes to specified U.S.-origin goods from September 8, according to the order’s schedules. Its October 23 update clarifies exemptions involving Chapters 98 and 99.

records.title: September 2026 Canada–U.S. merchandise trade snapshot
records.changed: September goods exports to the U.S. were C$55,169.8 million and imports C$42,836.8 million, up 0.7% and 0.4% from August. January–September exports rose 8.9% and imports 6.4% versus the same 2025 period.

records.title: Food security and agricultural diversification
records.changed: The Asia Pacific Foundation of Canada examines opportunities for food trade and agricultural cooperation, including technology and supply resilience.

records.title: China market access extended for four Canadian products
records.changed: Canada announced an agreement to continue favourable access for canola meal, peas, lobster and crab through the end of 2028. Canada also announced that it would extend certain steel and aluminum remissions through 2028.

records.title: September 2026: Canadian goods trade with the U.S. and China
records.changed: Canadian merchandise exports reached C$55.170 billion to the U.S. and C$4.448 billion to China, up 20.4% and 67.3% respectively from September 2025. Imports were C$42.837 billion from the U.S. and C$5.916 billion from China.

records.title: September energy export growth and the price effect
records.changed: Canadian energy product export values rose 8.2% from August to September; crude oil and bitumen rose 10.2%, driven by higher prices. Energy exports fell 5.0% over the third quarter.

records.title: September 2026: U.S. goods trade with China
records.changed: The U.S. Census Bureau reported US$9.614 billion in goods exports to China and US$31.485 billion in imports from China in September, compared with US$8.731 billion and US$27.134 billion in August.

records.title: First Canada–China ministerial energy dialogue
records.changed: Ministers met under the renewed partnership and identified conventional and renewable energy, civil nuclear energy and uranium as areas for further exchange.

records.title: First Canada–China investment working group meeting
records.changed: China’s Ministry of Commerce reported that Canadian and Chinese officials met in Ottawa to discuss investment policy and two-way investment.

records.title: U.S.–China Board of Trade: 30-for-30 recommendations
records.changed: U.S. and Chinese officials published a framework and lists for potential reciprocal tariff reductions on about US$30 billion of products in each direction, valued using 2024 trade.

records.title: PIIE benchmark: average U.S.–China tariffs
records.changed: The Peterson Institute’s series estimated average U.S. tariffs on Chinese goods at 35.2% and China’s on U.S. goods at 31.9% on August 22, 2026.

records.title: CUSMA joint review meeting
records.changed: Ministers met at the CUSMA Free Trade Commission for the agreement’s scheduled joint review.

records.title: Canada–China Financial Working Group launch
records.changed: Canadian and Chinese authorities held the first working group meeting and convened a roundtable with financial institutions.

records.title: Canada–China EV quota and agricultural measures take effect
records.changed: Canada implemented a 49,000-vehicle initial annual quota at the 6.1% rate for eligible China-origin EVs. China lowered the combined canola-seed tariff to 14.9% and suspended selected additional agri-food tariffs.

records.title: Canada–China energy cooperation MOU
records.changed: The leaders’ joint statement lists an energy cooperation MOU signed by Natural Resources Canada and China’s National Energy Administration.

records.title: Canada–China food safety and animal and plant health MOU
records.changed: Canadian and Chinese food inspection authorities signed a cooperation MOU on food safety and animal and plant health.

records.title: RCMP–China public security cooperation MOU
records.changed: The leaders’ joint statement lists a signed RCMP–China Ministry of Public Security MOU on combating crime and sets out cooperation on transnational crime and illegal synthetic drugs.

records.title: Modern wood construction MOU with British Columbia
records.changed: Canada, British Columbia and China signed a cooperation MOU on modern wood construction, with technical exchange identified in the trade roadmap.

records.title: Canada launches its Indo-Pacific Strategy
records.changed: Canada published a regional strategy covering economic engagement, diversification and security.

records.title: CUSMA enters into force
records.changed: CUSMA entered into force on July 1, 2020.

records.title: Canada–U.S. critical minerals action plan
records.changed: Canada and the United States finalized a joint action plan for critical minerals cooperation.

records.title: First U.S. Section 301 tariffs on covered Chinese goods
records.changed: The first U.S. tranche imposed an additional 25% duty on covered Chinese products from July 6, 2018.

records.title: Canada–China finance MOU and regulatory dialogue
records.changed: At the November 8–9 Vancouver dialogue, authorities signed a finance-ministry cooperation MOU, a financial-supervision dialogue agreement and financial working-group terms of reference.

records.title: New Canada–China business and university MOUs
records.changed: The Prime Minister’s release reports a CEO Roundtable MOU led by the Canada-China Business Council and Bank of China, and a uOttawa–SISU dual-degree MOU.

records.title: Expanded China tariff relief: next implementation gate is January 2027
records.changed: Canada announced additional relief for covered pork and seafood and longer steel/aluminum remissions. The updated backgrounder specifies removal of China’s additional 25% tariffs on listed products from January 1, 2027 through December 31, 2028.

records.title: Updated Canadian backgrounder reports shipments and EV arrivals
records.changed: The backgrounder updated November 20 reports C$1.74 billion in canola-seed exports in March–August 2026, up 43% from the same 2025 period, and 16,211 EV imports since March.

records.title: USTR presses China on purchases and critical-mineral commitments
records.changed: USTR’s November 6 readout says Greer and Bessent discussed implementation with He Lifeng, focusing on agricultural purchases, rare earths and other critical minerals.

records.title: China’s ministry reports its position on U.S.–China implementation
records.changed: In a November 12 press-conference response listed November 17, MOFCOM said China had implemented earlier consultation consensus and remained willing to manage differences through the consultation mechanism.

records.title: Canada’s trade advisory committee reviews tariffs and business support
records.changed: The November 19 committee readout reports discussion of ongoing U.S. trade talks, regional business pressures and the effectiveness of federal tariff-related supports.

records.title: Canada implements expanded U.S. surtax remission
records.changed: SOR/2026-235 was registered November 5, took effect November 9 and was published in the November 18 Gazette. It extends and expands eligible remission, including public education and specified mining and energy uses. Finance identifies later exclusions for certain trailers and aluminum/paperboard products.

records.title: U.S., Russia and China issue a security declaration
records.changed: The White House published a trilateral declaration covering dialogue on strategic security, nuclear risks and other cooperation.

records.title: The Plan for a Stronger Canada
records.changed: The October plan identifies eight strategic capabilities supported by economic security, foreign policy, defence policy, public safety and intelligence.

records.title: Spring Economic Update 2026: fiscal context
records.changed: The update announces an initial C$25B over three years, on a cash basis, for the Canada Strong Fund. It also describes auto support, trade infrastructure and defence ambitions.

records.title: Canada–ASEAN: negotiations substantially concluded
records.changed: The joint statement reports substantial conclusion of textual negotiations. Technical work remains and signing is targeted for 2027.

records.title: Canada–Indonesia agreement: scheduled entry into force
records.changed: The signed agreement is scheduled to enter into force on 1 December 2026.

records.title: Defence Industrial Strategy: capacity and delivery
records.changed: The February strategy prioritizes domestic industrial capacity and trusted-partner cooperation.

records.title: September 2026: production inputs and export concentration
records.changed: Vehicle and parts export values fell 4.9% from August. Computer and peripheral import values rose 29.4%, mainly processing units from the U.S. for data centres. Non-U.S. destinations received 29.8% of goods exports, versus 30.1% in August.

records.title: McIlvenna Bay: first mineral output and reported workforce
records.changed: Natural Resources Canada reports first copper concentrate in June 2026, followed by zinc and pyrite concentrates in July, and approximately 380 full-time workers at the September release.

records.title: CCC reports five-year U.S. contract for Canadian T400 engine parts
records.changed: CCC reports a five-year U.S. military award for T400 spare parts supplied by Pratt & Whitney Canada.

records.title: USTR extends suspension of covered maritime Section 301 measures
records.changed: A published Federal Register notice extends the suspension of the covered maritime measures from November 9, 2026 through 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on January 9, 2027.
